steps: Bring water to a boil, then add rice, salt, and butter.
Cover, lower heat to simmer, and cook for 20 minutes.
Place rice in upper part of double boiler with half and half, sugar, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel.
Bring to boil over direct heat.
Place over simmering water in double boiler and cook for 45 minutes.
Remove cinnamon stick and lemon peel.
Pour rice mixture into a 2-quart (1.9 L) casserole and allow to cool.
Sprinkle with cinnamon powder.

ingredients: 2–3 tbsp white granulated sugar, or to taste
200 g butter, soft margarine, or shortening
steps: Combine flour, baking powder, sugar and salt and make a well in the center.
Add some water to the well and mix by hand. Gradually knead in remaining water, then knead 15 minutes; dough should not be too soft or sticky.
Tear off fist-sized pieces, flatten and roll out, then shape into balls. Brush all balls thinly with oil.
Rest for 1–2 hours until slightly sunken.
Roll and stretch each ball on a greased surface as thin as possible without tearing.

Spread soft butter over the entire surface. Fold one-third lengthwise toward the middle, then fold over the other side. Make a small fold up and down, then roll from bottom to top with greased hands like a sleeping bag, forming an elongated fat roll. Repeat for all balls.
Preheat oven to 212°F (100°C). Line a pot with bread or pita slices.
Place unbaked jachnun in cookie bags, a single layer per bag. Stack 2–3 rows in the pot, alternating horizontally and vertically.
Cover and bake for 6–10 hours.
Serve with hard-boiled eggs, tomato salsa and a little zhug.

ingredients: 2 handfuls crushed dried red chile peppers
½ lb (225 g) finely chopped garlic
steps: Sear beef in a little cooking oil, not lard, until lightly browned. Put beef and chile peppers in a large stock pot with enough water to prevent burning. Bring to a boil, then lower heat, cover and simmer about 30 minutes.

Remove from stove and add spices and garlic. Return to stove, bring to a boil, lower heat and simmer another 90 minutes, keeping covered as much as possible. Stir only as necessary to avoid tearing the meat. Add as little additional water as needed to prevent burning.
Remove from heat, skim off all or most grease, and serve hot.
